title: Does the factory catalogue count as seeing the part
ask: Does a part the factory catalogue lists for this car, on a system nothing has changed, count as a fact about the car now without you looking at it?
why: The Manual (D-417) shows a part only when nothing about it says confirm. 237 parts are held today for that word alone, and for about 182 of them the doubt is not a measurement but 'is this internal factory part still fitted?' - an oil pan, an eccentric shaft, a brush holder - written by the catalogue transcription because nobody has looked. Each became one of your 290 verify rows ('Is the Oil pan (PT077) on the car as described?'), most of them about parts you cannot see without taking something apart. Meanwhile the Manual hides 28 % of the parts list. Whether a part the factory catalogue lists for this chassis (fits=yes), on a system nothing has changed, counts as a fact about your car without you looking at it is your bar (your spec answer 4.5), not the agent's; it decides how many of the 290 taps exist.
options:
(a) Yes: a fits=yes catalogue row on a system nothing has changed is backed. 'confirm' stays only where a known change touches the system (the carburettor and air cleaner, emissions, the removed metering pump, the optional equipment you have already ruled on) or the scan was unreadable. The B-K rows for the rest are dropped - roughly 200 fewer taps - and the Manual shows those parts marked 'from the factory catalogue, not yet seen'.
(b) No: every part is seen before it is shown. The 290 rows stay (at a minute a row, about five hours of tapping across several sessions), and the Manual fills in as you go.
(c) Yes for what cannot be seen without disassembly (inside the engine, gearbox, axles, doors); no for what is visible from the driveway or under the hood, which stays on your list. Roughly halves the list.
recommend: (a), unless you want the Manual to show only what you have personally seen - then (c).
stops: Plan step P29 (collapsing the verify list) and how many of the 290 rows remain.

title: Check the factory harness before it comes out?
ask: Should the 80 wiring-check rows - unplug each factory connector and check its terminals' labels and wire colours against the 1982 diagram - be done at all, when the electrical project replaces the harness?
why: Eighty of your verify rows (stage W) ask you to unplug a factory connector and check each terminal's label and wire colour against the 1982 wiring diagram - 401 terminals across 80 devices, 36 of them with no known colour to compare against. The electrical project replaces the whole harness (D-211, D-411: the factory harness comes out while the car is apart), so the wire colours you would write down go in the bin with it. What survives the rebuild is the devices themselves - the alternator, starter, motors, switches, senders the new legs plug into - and their terminal labels matter for pinning the new harness; their old wire colours do not. Whether to check the factory harness at all is scope, so it is your call; until you rule, the 80 rows are gated on this block and off your list.
options:
(a) Drop all 80 rows. The 426 researched terminals stay in the record as 'from the 1982 diagram, unchecked' and nobody unplugs anything for a harness that is leaving. Costs nothing; forecloses nothing, because every device gets its terminals checked anyway when the new leg is pinned to it (the build rows E20-E23).
(b) Keep only the rows for devices that survive the rebuild (roughly a third), and do each one when that device is in your hand during the strip and build - gated on 01-electrical:S1. The terminal labels are confirmed where they matter; the wire colours are noted only if they happen to be in view.
(c) Keep all 80 as they are, to be done at the strip when every connector is unplugged anyway. The most complete check of the factory diagram, at the cost of a weekend of looking at wires that are being thrown away.
recommend: (a), unless you want the terminal labels of the devices that survive confirmed before the new legs are pinned - then (b).
stops: Nothing today: the 80 stage-W rows wait on this block.
